doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Classical teacher Eva Wasserman and saxophone ideas on clarinet
summary: Her classical teacher supported her move to jazz; her sax studies and Illinois Jacquet shaped her clarinet playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Would your, I assume you had a classical clarinet teacher early on, and I wonder if they saw you playing on a video, I noticed the one thing I was going to ask you about next, a video with Paquito D’Rivera, and at one point you took, I guess it was your left hand and you put it down at your side while you were playing. Now, and also during this particular solo, you used some lovely vibrato. So I’m wondering if your classical teacher might have looked at that and go oh Anat, you shouldn’t be doing that?

Well my classical teacher, I had one main teacher when I was, before I transformed into jazz life, when I was studying a little bit of classical clarinet and her name is Eva Wasserman, she still lives in Israel. And she has been very supportive of my path and she calls me up and she’s proud of me, and she saw me early on moving away from that strict, strictly classical world and she supported it. And she never made a comment that something is wrong. But it’s always interesting, you know I think years of playing saxophone invaded into my clarinet playing. So what I allowed myself to study and to practice on the saxophone I allow myself to do on the clarinet. So maybe it’s not strictly a clarinet approach and not something that a clarinet teacher might teach you, but that’s something that Illinois Jacquet inspired me to play on the tenor saxophone and I’m like okay, I just happened to hold a different horn but the music is, it’s not about the instrument it’s about what’s inside.
